content: Nelfinavir increases the level or effect of other drugs by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. This interaction can lead to significant changes in drug efficacy and safety, requiring careful monitoring and potential dose adjustments. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Nelfinavir and Gastric pH Modifiers: Drugs that increase gastric pH, such as ibuprofen/famotidine, can reduce the absorption and effectiveness of nelfinavir. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Fedratinib: Fedratinib increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Dose adjustments for CYP2C19 substrates may be necessary. Monitor closely. 3. Felodipine: Nelfinavir increases felodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while felodipine increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 4. Fesoterodine: Nelfinavir increases fesoterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 5. Fexinidazole: Fexinidazole increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Fluconazole: Fluconazole increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Fludrocortisone: Nelfinavir increases fludrocortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Flunisolide (Inhaled): Nelfinavir increases flunisolide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Flurazepam: Nelfinavir increases flurazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider lowering benzodiazepine doses, using alternatives if available, and monitor closely. 10. Fluticasone Furoate and Fluticasone (Inhaled): Nelfinavir increases fluticasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. Use caution and monitor. 11. Fluvastatin: Nelfinavir increases fluvastatin toxicity through OATP1B1 inhibition, raising the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 12. Fluvoxamine: Fluvoxamine increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Fosamprenavir: Fosamprenavir increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and nelfinavir increases fosamprenavir levels similarly. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 14. Fosaprepitant: Fosaprepitant increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and nelfinavir increases fosaprepitant levels similarly. Use caution and monitor. 15. Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases nelfinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Use caution and monitor. 16. Fostamatinib: Nelfinavir increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and fostamatinib increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely for toxicities and consider dose reductions. 17. Garlic: Garlic decreases nelfinavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Gefitinib: Nelfinavir increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 19. Givinostat: Both nelfinavir and givinostat prolong the QTc interval. Obtain ECGs at baseline, during coadministration, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if QTc >500 ms or if there is a >60 ms change from baseline. 20. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Nelfinavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir also increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 21. Glimepiride, Glipizide, Glyburide: Nelfinavir decreases the effects of these drugs due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors, leading to hyperglycemia. Use caution and monitor. 22. Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Griseofulvin: Griseofulvin decreases nelfinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Guanfacine: Nelfinavir increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce guanfacine dosage by half for extended-release formulations when coadministered. Monitor closely for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 25. Haloperidol: Nelfinavir increases haloperidol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Hydrocodone: Nelfinavir increases hydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may result in fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 27. Hydrocortisone: Nelfinavir increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Nelfinavir increases hydroxyprogesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Ifosfamide: Nelfinavir decreases ifosfamide levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism, potentially reducing therapeutic effects. Use caution and monitor. 30. Iloperidone: Nelfinavir increases iloperidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone also increases nelfinavir levels as a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor. Monitor closely. 31. Imipramine: Nelfinavir increases imipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Indacaterol (Inhaled): Nelfinavir increases indacaterol levels by modulating P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activity. No dose adjustment is required at the 75 mcg dose. Use caution and monitor. 33. Indinavir: Indinavir increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 34. Insulin (Various Types): Nelfinavir decreases the effects of insulin (e.g., aspart, detemir, glargine, lispro) due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors, leading to hyperglycemia. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 35. Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Istradefylline: Nelfinavir increases istradefylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Reduce istradefylline dose to 20 mg/day when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 37. Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 38. Ivacaftor: Nelfinavir increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce ivacaftor dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 39. Ixabepilone: Nelfinavir increases ixabepilone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Ketamine: Nelfinavir decreases ketamine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 41. Ketoconazole: Ketoconazole increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Use caution and monitor. 42. Lacosamide: Nelfinavir and lacosamide increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing lacosamide dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 43. Lamivudine: Both nelfinavir and lamivudine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 44. Lapatinib: Nelfinavir increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lapatinib increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 45. Lenacapavir: Lenacapavir increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse reactions. 46. Letermovir: Nelfinavir increases letermovir levels by decreasing metabolism, and letermovir increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Levamlodipine: Nelfinavir increases levamlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema, and adjust the dose as needed. 48. LevoKetoconazole: LevoKetoconazole increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Use caution and monitor. 49. Levomilnacipran: Nelfinavir increases levomilnacipran levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 50. Linagliptin: Nelfinavir decreases linagliptin effects due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor.
